title: Your first floating window.
dek: Keep a checklist, a set of instructions, or a local report beside the work. Start with a file you already have.
label: 01 / Getting started

margin.title: What you need
margin.text: VS Code desktop 1.134.0 or later, Porthole, and a local HTML or Markdown file. The latest VS Code release is officially supported.

margin.title: Tested on macOS
margin.text: Porthole has been run on macOS. Windows and Linux have not yet been tested.

margin.title: A first-use question
margin.text: Porthole may ask whether VS Code should keep floating windows to one tab. Keep Compact, Not Now, and Don’t Ask Again let you choose.

title: Choose the page for the job.
dek: Use Markdown for notes and reference material. Use HTML when the page needs buttons, fields, or checkboxes you can click.
label: 02 / Working with pages

margin.title: Local files
margin.text: Supported extensions are .html, .htm, .md, and .markdown. Web addresses, localhost URLs, remote workspaces, and virtual workspaces are outside the supported scope.

margin.title: Markdown verification
margin.text: Markdown was tested on VS Code 1.141.0. The necessary preview editor appears in the source for 1.134.0, but Markdown was not tested on that version.

margin.title: A small canvas
margin.text: An HTML page about 420–640 pixels wide is a useful starting point. Keep instructions readable without scrolling sideways.

title: Shape the window.
dek: Choose a size, keep the page above your other windows, and return it to the main VS Code window.
label: 03 / Size, position, and focus

margin.title: Focus first
margin.text: Click the floating window before using its size, pin, or dock command. With several windows open, make the intended window active.

margin.title: Minimum size
margin.text: VS Code will not make the window smaller than 400 × 270 pixels. The default presets are 420 × 640, 480 × 720, and 640 × 900.

margin.title: Exact sizes
margin.text: Preset sizing relies on an internal VS Code command. If it fails, Porthole tries another way to open the window, without applying the requested size.

title: Open a page from a terminal.
dek: Write the page to disk. Send its local path to VS Code with a vscode:// link.
label: 04 / Outside links · Experimental

margin.title: Experimental
margin.text: Outside links have been run on macOS in VS Code. Their shape may change; check the changelog when upgrading.

margin.title: Version requirements
margin.text: Opening from an outside link requires Porthole 0.3.0 or later. Installing the model skill through the extension requires 0.4.0 or later.

margin.title: One receiving window
margin.text: The VS Code window used most recently receives the link. A repo parameter selects a workspace folder within that window; it does not route the link to another window.

title: Settings and troubleshooting.
dek: Change window settings and outside-link permissions. Check the Porthole output channel when a command or link does not work.
label: 05 / Settings and troubleshooting

margin.title: Find the settings
margin.text: Open VS Code Settings and search for porthole. The tables show the defaults shipped in Porthole 0.4.0.

margin.title: Read Porthole’s logs
margin.text: Open VS Code’s Output panel and select Porthole. Refused links and internal-command fallbacks are reported there.

margin.title: When reporting a problem
margin.text: Include your VS Code version and the Porthole output. If you use an older VS Code release, first try the latest version.
